label: Single dyes
detected
stations.title: Single fluorescent dyes detected directly
stations.cite: First direct detection of single dye tags, 1990
stations.text: Single fluorescent dye molecules were detected directly for the first time. Every later single-molecule fluorescence method, including smFRET, builds on this.

label: Myosin ATPase
Funatsu et al.
stations.title: ATP turnover by single myosin molecules
stations.text: The first biological application of single-molecule fluorescence imaging, in vitro with total internal reflection excitation.

label: First smFRET
Ha et al.
stations.title: First single-molecule FRET
stations.text: FRET measured on individual, doubly labelled DNA molecules. It showed that donor–acceptor energy transfer can report distances and fluctuations one molecule at a time.

label: Membrane ligands
Schütz et al.
stations.title: Ligands on receptors in a membrane
stations.text: Single-molecule FRET and colocalization used to watch ligand binding to streptavidin immobilised on phospholipid membranes. Later reviews describe it as the step that opened the way to live-cell experiments.

label: EGF receptors
Sako et al.
stations.title: Single molecules imaged in living cells
stations.cite: Sako, Minoghchi & Yanagida, Nat Cell Biol 2, 168–172, 2000
stations.text: The first single-molecule fluorescence imaging in live cells: fluorescent EGF and EGF receptors followed on the cell surface by total internal reflection microscopy, with FRET used to look at receptor signalling.

label: Ras activation
Murakoshi et al.
stations.title: Ras activation on the cell membrane
stations.text: Single-molecule imaging of Ras activation in living cells, extending the Yanagida group's surface-imaging approach to a signalling protein.

label: SNARE folding
Sakon & Weninger
stations.title: Conformation of individual proteins in live cells
stations.text: Recombinant SNARE proteins, site-specifically labelled with donor and acceptor, were microinjected into cultured cells. smFRET combined with single-particle tracking showed single proteins folding into complexes at the cell membrane.

label: Electroporation
Crawford et al.
stations.title: Loading labelled molecules into live E. coli
stations.text: Electroporation introduced dye-labelled DNA and proteins into live bacteria and gave long-lived single-molecule fluorescence, the start of in vivo smFRET in bacteria.

label: In-cell dyes
Plochowietz et al.
stations.title: Which dyes survive inside a cell
stations.cite: Plochowietz, Crawford & Kapanidis, Phys Chem Chem Phys 16, 12688, 2014
stations.text: Several donor and acceptor dyes were compared in live E. coli. Cy3B, ATTO 647 and ATTO 647N performed best for brightness and photostability.

label: Confocal in cells
König et al.
stations.title: Single-molecule spectroscopy in live eukaryotic cells
stations.text: Confocal smFRET in live mammalian cells with improved delivery and cell culture conditions, probing dynamics from milliseconds to nanoseconds. Applications included an intrinsically disordered protein, in-cell cold denaturation and protein folding.

label: Ruler to the jungle
Sustarsic &
Kapanidis
stations.title: Taking the ruler to the jungle
stations.cite: Sustarsic & Kapanidis, Curr Opin Struct Biol, 2015
stations.text: Review of smFRET for biomolecular structure and dynamics in live cells, covering delivery, labelling and the open methodological problems.

label: End-sealed DNA
Plochowietz et al.
stations.title: Stable DNA rulers for in vivo smFRET
stations.cite: Plochowietz, El-Sagheer, Brown & Kapanidis, Chem Sci 7, 2016
stations.text: DNA standards with chemically sealed ends survive inside live bacteria and give smFRET signals of about 10 s. Multi-dye versions extend fluorescence signals to about 1 min, giving a quality check for in vivo workflows.

label: Benchmark study
Hellenkamp et al.
stations.title: Multi-laboratory smFRET benchmark
stations.text: Precision and accuracy of smFRET measured across many laboratories, in vitro. It sets the reference level that live-cell measurements are compared against.

label: Two decades
Lerner et al.
stations.title: Two decades of smFRET
stations.text: Review of 22 years of smFRET in structural and molecular biology. It notes that most work was in vitro, with live-cell use emerging.

label: mGluR2 in cells
Asher et al.
stations.title: smFRET of GPCR dimers in living cells
stations.text: Wide-field smFRET with single-particle tracking followed assembly and conformational dynamics of metabotropic glutamate receptors in the plasma membrane. A commentary calls it the first view of membrane-protein structural dynamics (mGluR2) in living cells.

label: Auto-analysis
Frontiers 2023
stations.title: Automated analysis of live-cell smFRET
stations.cite: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology, 2023
stations.text: An automated pipeline for live-cell smFRET trajectories, built on smCellFRET and machine vision, tested on mGluR2 with an LDL-TM monomer as negative control.

label: Nettels & Schuler
Nat Rev Phys
stations.title: smFRET for nanoscale biomolecular dynamics
stations.text: State-of-the-art review covering time resolution, nonequilibrium dynamics and the physics-based developments expected to extend the method.

label: FRET-TTB
Anandamurugan et al.
stations.title: Tracking transfected proteins by smFRET
stations.text: Long-term smFRET of the cytosolic chaperone Hsp90, using HILO microscopy, ALEX-based detection, dual-channel tracking and protein transfection. End-sealed DNA standards validated the method against in vitro data.

label: RAF in cells
Frontiers 2025
stations.title: In-cell smFRET of cytosolic RAF proteins
stations.text: Confocal ALEX-smFRET in cells to read structural states and kinetics of CRAF and BRAF in their native environment. CRAF showed three structural states; wild-type BRAF mostly one.

label: MET receptors
Li et al.
stations.title: FRET-tracking of MET receptor activation
stations.text: smFRET recovery after photobleaching, combined with single-particle tracking, detected ligand-induced dimerisation and dimer–monomer transitions of the MET receptor in living cells.

links.note: FRET-TTB validated its method with end-sealed DNA, the standard type described in 2016. That the paper cites the 2016 work was not confirmed.
